title: Accessibility of the colimit closure of a small compact family
statement: Use the fixed nested universes, smallness, local smallness, infinite regular cardinals, $\kappa$-compactness and accessibility from [def-coef-presentable-infinity-category] and coherent diagrams, full subcategories, equivalences and colimits from [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Let $\kappa$ be an uncountable regular cardinal in the smaller universe, let $\mathcal E$ be a locally small infinity category admitting all small colimits, and let $G$ be a small set of $\kappa$-compact objects of $\mathcal E$. There is a replete full subcategory $\mathcal H\subseteq\mathcal E$ containing $G$ with the following properties. It is closed under all small colimits computed in $\mathcal E$ (the empty colimit is included), and it is $\kappa$-accessible. Its inclusion preserves all small colimits. More precisely, there is an essentially small full subcategory $\mathcal A\subseteq\mathcal H$ of objects that are $\kappa$-compact in $\mathcal E$ such that every object of $\mathcal H$ is a small $\kappa$-filtered colimit in $\mathcal E$ of objects of $\mathcal A$. The subcategory $\mathcal H$ is minimal with respect to containing $G$, being replete and being closed under small colimits. Replete means closed under equivalence in $\mathcal E$.

source.place: Theorem 5.5.1.1, proof of (6) implies (1), printed pp. 458-460, for the compact-generation construction; Corollary 5.3.4.15 for compactness of kappa-small colimits; Propositions 5.3.5.10 and 5.3.5.11(1), printed pp. 406-407, for extension into a category admitting filtered colimits and its full faithfulness; Corollary 5.3.5.4(3), printed p. 404, for the restricted-Yoneda right adjoint and hence ambient colimit preservation. The hull formulation is an agent-formulated consequence, not a verbatim statement of Theorem 5.5.1.1. No ambient presentability is used. This is the general compact-generation input to Gepner–Haugseng Proposition A.5.9. No Stacks tag states this infinity-categorical result.
